extracted.intended_audience: PR professionals, communications teams, startup founders and anyone writing press releases for journalists
extracted.subtask_description: A practical, journalist-focused press release template and checklist for drafting news-first releases that reporters will scan and potentially use. Emphasizes concise lede, defined paragraph roles, substantive quotes, and required contact/boilerplate elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard header format
rubrics_metrics.description:
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE / EMBARGOED UNTIL [date/time]
[CITY, State / Country] — [Date]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this industry-standard header so reporters can immediately see release timing and location; include EMBARGOED WHEN APPLICABLE. 'Why: Standard format reporters scan for' — follow this exact convention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline length and news-first
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep headlines to roughly 8–12 words and make the news explicit (lead with the result/impact). Avoid vague or promotional language; example anti-pattern: 'Acme Corp Unveils Revolutionary Solution' should be rewritten to state the measurable news (e.g., 'Acme Corp Cuts Wait Times 50% With New Software').

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional subheadline expands on news
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a short subheadline only when it adds concrete information or context that complements the headline rather than repeating it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lede: 5 W's compressed into ~50 words
rubrics_metrics.description:
[Company/Person] today announced [news] that [why it matters].
[Specific detail: number, date, named entity].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The lede should answer who, what, when, where, why (and sometimes how) in about 50 words. Include at least one specific detail (a number, date, or named entity) to make the announcement tangible. 'Why: 5 W's compressed into 50 words.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Body length and paragraph count
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the main body short — no more than 2–4 paragraphs beyond the lede. Reporters prefer concise releases; excess length reduces pick-up likelihood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Body paragraph roles and order
rubrics_metrics.description:
Para 2: Context — why this matters in the broader market
Para 3: Quote from C-level spokesperson (substantive, not generic)
Para 4: Specifics — methodology, timeline, partners
Para 5 (optional): Customer/partner quote
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the suggested paragraph sequencing so the release flows from immediate news to context to verification (quotes) to concrete details. Use Para 5 only if it adds new, relevant perspective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive quote from named spokesperson
rubrics_metrics.description: Quote from C-level spokesperson (substantive, not generic)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a meaningful, attributable quote (named C-level or relevant spokesperson) that adds insight or interpretation, not filler. Avoid generic praise or platitudes — 'Quote that says nothing' is a common mistake. Quotes should provide information journalists can reuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specifics paragraph (methodology, timeline, partners)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide verifiable specifics such as how something works, when it will happen, partner organizations, metrics/methods. This paragraph should enable reporters to understand and fact-check the claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional customer or partner quote
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a customer or partner quote only if it adds independent validation or a distinct perspective; keep it short and substantive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boilerplate: concise company description (≈75 words)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a short (about 75 words) company background for unfamiliar readers. 'Why: Background for unfamiliar readers; under 75 words.' Avoid long, promotional boilerplates — 'Boilerplate that takes 200 words' is flagged as a mistake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Named media contact with phone (required)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List a single, named media contact. Include phone (REQUIRED) and email (secondary). Reporters expect one clear contact for follow-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry-standard end marker
rubrics_metrics.guidance: End the release with the standard '###' marker to signal the end of the release copy. 'Why: Industry standard "end of release" marker.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid filler opener phrases
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid lead phrases that add no news value. Journalists skip filler; begin with the actual news instead of promotional framing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headlines must contain tangible news/impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Mistake: Headline like "Acme Corp Unveils Revolutionary Solution"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't use marketing-superlative headlines that hide the actual result. Rewrite headlines to state the measurable change or concrete benefit (e.g., include percent changes, dates, counts, named partners).
